findings.explanation: Splunk's add-on documentation says the add-on assigns all Cisco UCS data the sourcetype `cisco:ucs` and sets the source per class ID, so faultInst events arrive as `sourcetype=cisco:ucs source=cisco:ucs:faultInst`. A `cisco:ucs:faults` sourcetype is not produced by the add-on.
findings.quote: sourcetype `cisco:ucs:faults` from the Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS (Splunkbase 2731, v4.3.1). The TA’s **modular input** polls the UCS Manager XML/HTTPS **API** and materialises `faultInst` into indexed events
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the feed as `index=cisco_ucs sourcetype=cisco:ucs source=cisco:ucs:faultInst`, collected by an add-on Input that uses a Template containing the faultInst class ID. Only mention a custom sourcetype if the site overrides it on the Input.

findings.explanation: This gets it backwards. The add-on's documented install path is `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs/` and the Splunkbase package name is `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs`. The current release is 4.3.3 (compatible with 9.1 through 10.5). 4.3.1 only supported Splunk 9.1 through 9.4.
findings.quote: current release 4.3.1, Splunk-supported on 9.1–10.2 and Splunk Cloud). The install directory and Splunkbase package name are `Splunk_TA_cisco_ucs` (underscore). Older download bundles may still show the hyphenated `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs` string—treat that as a filename artefact
findings.suggested_fix: State that the package and folder name is `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs` (hyphen), the current release is 4.3.3, and give the Splunk compatibility from the release notes (4.3.3 supports 9.1.x through 10.5.x).

findings.explanation: F0479 is fltDcxVIfLinkState (virtual interface link down, cause vif-down), not a memory fault. F0408 is fltEquipmentChassisPowerProblem (chassis power state against the power policy), not PSU input. The memory example in Step 3 (`.../mem-4/fault-F0479`) inherits the same error.
findings.quote: examples you can bookmark while testing: **F0479** for memory, **F0521** for CPU thermal, **F0408** for PSU input
findings.suggested_fix: Use real codes from the Cisco UCS Faults Reference, for example F0184/F0185 (fltMemoryUnitDegraded / fltMemoryUnitInoperable) for memory, F0175–F0177 for processor thermal, and F0408 described as chassis power problem. Fix the Step 3 example DN to a memory fault code.

findings.explanation: UCSM syslog is configured under Admin > All > Faults, Events, and Audit Log > Syslog. Communication Services holds HTTP/HTTPS, SNMP, and similar services. The Local Sources there are Faults, Events, and Audits, not 'fault and equipment classes'.
findings.quote: in UCSM choose **Admin > Communication & Management > Communication Services** (wording can vary by 3.x/4.x) and configure a **syslog** destination
findings.suggested_fix: Use Admin > All > Faults, Events, and Audit Log > Syslog. Configure a Remote Destination with level and facility, and enable the Faults (and optionally Audits/Events) local sources.

findings.explanation: The add-on is configured as Managers (splunk_ta_cisco_ucs_servers.conf), Templates of class IDs (splunk_ta_cisco_ucs_templates.conf), and Inputs that bind managers and templates. Collection runs on a heavy forwarder only. Copying a `cisco_ucs://` stanza is not the documented workflow.
findings.quote: open `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/Splunk_TA_cisco_ucs/default/inputs.conf` and copy the **documented** stanza template for the Cisco UCS family (naming is commonly `cisco_ucs://<label>`
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the documented flow: add a Manager (host and read-only credentials), make sure a Template includes `faultInst`, create an Input that selects the manager and template with an interval and index, then confirm with `index=cisco_ucs sourcetype=cisco:ucs source=cisco:ucs:faultInst`.

findings.explanation: dataSources and detailedImplementation suggest syslog lines can be parsed into the same fault sourcetype. However, UCSM syslog lines do not carry the XML faultInst attributes (`lc`, `ack`, `created`, `occur`) the SPL relies on, and the subcategory guide keeps syslog as a separate `cisco:ucs:syslog` sourcetype. The Step 1 advice to set props/transforms on a Universal Forwarder would also not parse the stream.
findings.quote: **or** you forward **UCSM syslog** to a receiver that normalises the same logical sourcetype
findings.suggested_fix: Present syslog as a separate, complementary sourcetype with its own extractions on the heavy forwarder or SC4S tier. State that the SPL as written only works on the API-polled faultInst events.

findings.explanation: The reference URL is the Cisco home path, not the faults reference its title promises.
findings.quote:
"title": "Cisco UCS Faults Reference, Release 4.2 (fault codes, causes, actions)",
      "url": "https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/"
findings.suggested_fix: Link the actual Cisco UCS Faults and Error Messages Reference page for the UCSM release in scope.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by a generic org handle, yet it contains a non-existent sourcetype, wrong fault codes and a wrong GUI path, so the claim of SME verification is not supported.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade to a draft or community status until a named SME validates it against a live add-on deployment.

findings.explanation: Sorting does not fix anything. The sentence muddles what the detection does: it lists open hardware faults per server part so staff can replace the part before redundancy is lost.
findings.quote: We sort by that path so a fan, power unit, or memory bank is fixed while redundancy still holds
findings.suggested_fix: Say plainly: we list every open hardware fault on each Cisco blade or rack server, grouped by the part affected (fan, power supply, memory, disk), so the team can replace it before a second failure causes an outage.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The search filters `sourcetype="cisco:ucs:faults"`, which the Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS does not produce. The add-on writes `sourcetype=cisco:ucs` with `source=cisco:ucs:faultInst`, so the search returns nothing on a default install. Use `sourcetype=cisco:ucs source="cisco:ucs:faultInst"`.

`sort 0 - count, - severity` sorts severity as a string (warning > minor > major > critical), so critical rows sort last among equal counts. Also, each poll re-ingests the same open fault, so `count` measures poll repetitions over 24h rather than distinct faults. Map severity to a rank (for example with the add-on's `ucs_fault_highestSeverity` lookup) and use dc or latest instead.

summary: The detailed implementation is substantive, but the UC is built on a sourcetype the Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS does not emit (the add-on uses sourcetype cisco:ucs with source cisco:ucs:faultInst), misstates the add-on folder name and version support, cites a wrong fault code for memory, and gives a wrong UCSM syslog navigation path.
